# SDK map — UnivaPay TypeScript SDK v3 (`univapay-client-sdk@1.2.3`)

Use this map to look things up instead of reading the SDK source: what to call, with which arguments in which order, what each argument is called on the wire, what comes back, and what is thrown. Read this page once. Then open only the one operation page you need; it links to the model tables it uses.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Package | `univapay-client-sdk`, version `1.2.3` — install it pinned: `npm install --save-exact univapay-client-sdk@1.2.3` |
| Generator | APIMatic v3.0, plus hand-written code: `src/extensions.ts` (poll helpers, Idempotency-Key interceptor, token helpers) and hand edits in `src/client.ts` (controller getters, client shortcuts), `src/authProvider.ts`, `src/defaultConfiguration.ts` |
| Import | `import { Client } from 'univapay-client-sdk'` — the package root is the only entry that works (see Runtime & packaging) |
| HTTP transport | axios, through `@apimatic/axios-client-adapter` |
| Source paths | every `Source` path on these pages starts at the package root, e.g. `src/controllers/chargesApi.ts`. The package ships its `src/` folder, so the same path works inside `node_modules/univapay-client-sdk/` |

---

## Getting a client

```ts
import { Client } from 'univapay-client-sdk';

declare const appSecret: string; // the app token's secret
declare const appJwt: string; // the app token (JWT)

const client = new Client({
  bearerAuthCredentials: { secretKey: appSecret, jwtToken: appJwt },
});

const response = await client.refunds.getRefund('storeId', 'chargeId', 'refundId');
const refund = response.result; // Refund
```

- **Credentials.** `bearerAuthCredentials` takes `secretKey` and `jwtToken`. Every call sends `Authorization: Bearer <secretKey>.<jwtToken>`. Their README and `doc/` pages show `accessToken` instead; that name does not exist in the code.
- **No credentials.** `new Client()` builds fine, but every call then rejects with a plain `Error` ("Required authentication credentials for this API call are not provided ...") and nothing is sent.
- **Controllers.** The client has one getter per controller: `client.cancels`, `client.charges`, `client.checkout`, `client.directDebit`, `client.merchants`, `client.refunds`, `client.stores`, `client.subscriptions`, `client.transactionHistory`, `client.transactionTokens`, `client.webhooks`. Each getter returns the same instance every time. Building one yourself (`new RefundsApi(client)`) also works.
- **The app token's ids.** `client.getCurrentStoreId()` returns the `store_id` claim of `jwtToken` (store-level tokens only) and `client.getCurrentMerchantId()` returns the `merchant_id` claim (both token kinds). Each returns `null` when there is no token, the token is not a JWT, the claim is missing, or the claim is not a UUID. The signature is not checked.

`Configuration` fields (source: `src/configuration.ts`; every field is optional in the constructor):

| Field | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bearerAuthCredentials` | `{ secretKey: string; jwtToken: string }` | none |
| `baseUrl` | `string` | `https://api.univapay.com` |
| `directDebitBaseUrl` | `string` | `https://direct-debit.gopay-services.com` |
| `environment` | `Environment` — one member, `Environment.Production` | `Environment.Production` |
| `timeout` | `number` (ms) | `30000` |
| `httpClientOptions` | `Partial<HttpClientOptions>`: `timeout`, `retryConfig`, `proxySettings`, `httpAgent`, `httpsAgent` | none. `httpClientOptions.timeout`, when set, is used instead of `timeout` |
| `unstable_httpClientOptions` | `any` — handed to the axios adapter as `clientConfigOverrides` (`src/client.ts`) | none |
| `logging` | `PartialLoggingOptions` | none (nothing is logged) |

`baseUrl` and `directDebitBaseUrl` can point anywhere, a local test server included; a path after the host is kept.

`httpClientOptions.retryConfig` (type `RetryConfiguration`; defaults in `DEFAULT_RETRY_CONFIG`, `src/defaultConfiguration.ts`):

| Field | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `maxNumberOfRetries` | `0` | retries are **off** |
| `maximumRetryWaitTime` | `0` (seconds) | the total wait allowed across retries. **While it is 0, no retry happens even with `maxNumberOfRetries` above 0** |
| `retryInterval` | `1` (seconds) | first wait, multiplied by `backoffFactor` (`2`) each time |
| `httpMethodsToRetry` | `['GET', 'PUT', 'GET', 'PUT']` | POST, PATCH and DELETE are not retried unless listed |
| `httpStatusCodesToRetry` | `408, 413, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504, 521, 522, 524` (each listed twice) | see the trap below |
| `retryOnTimeout` | `true` | a call that ends in a thrown error — a timeout, or a status with a row in the error table — is retried only while this is `true` |

Retry trap: the SDK treats an error it throws itself like a timeout. So once retries are on, every status that has a row in the operation's error table — 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 429, 500, 503, 504 — is retried while `retryOnTimeout` is `true`, whatever `httpStatusCodesToRetry` says. With `retryOnTimeout: false` none of those is retried, not even 503; only statuses without a row that are in `httpStatusCodesToRetry` (for example 502) still are. A status with no row and not in the list (for example 418) is retried only when the response carries a `Retry-After` header above 0; then the SDK waits as the header says. For a status that has a row (429 included) `Retry-After` is ignored: the wait is `retryInterval × backoffFactor^n`. The three operations with no error rows (`createSubscription`, `listAllSubscriptions`, `listStoreSubscriptions`) follow only `httpStatusCodesToRetry` (and `Retry-After`): a 503 is retried there even with `retryOnTimeout: false`, and a 400 is not retried. A retried POST sends the same `Idempotency-Key` on every attempt.

**Other ways to build a client:**

- `Client.fromEnvironment(env?)` reads `SECRET_KEY` and `JWT_TOKEN` (both or neither — one alone throws "Both SECRET_KEY and JWT_TOKEN must be set together ..."), plus `BASE_URL`, `DIRECT_DEBIT_BASE_URL`, `TIMEOUT`, the retry, proxy and logging variables (`src/configuration.ts`). **A client from `fromEnvironment` always writes every request and response line to the console.** `LOG_LEVEL` only changes the label (`info:`, `error:` ...); it does not filter. To silence it: `Client.fromEnvironment(env).withConfiguration({ logging: undefined })`.
- `Client.fromJsonConfig(json)` is broken in 1.2.3: it throws `TypeError: schema.type is not a function`. Parse the JSON yourself and pass the object to `new Client(...)`.
- `client.withConfiguration(partial)` returns a new `Client` with the given fields replaced.

**Logging.** With no `logging` option nothing is logged. Any `logging` object, even `{}`, turns logging on: every request and response line goes to `console.log` (or to your `logger.log(level, message, params)`), labelled with `logLevel` (default `info`). `logLevel` never filters anything. With `logRequest: { logBody: true }` the request body, card data included, is written to the logger. With `logRequest: { logHeaders: true }` the headers are written too; the `Authorization` value is replaced by `**Redacted**` while `maskSensitiveHeaders` is `true` (the default). **With `maskSensitiveHeaders: false` the full `Bearer <secretKey>.<jwtToken>` is written** — never set it outside a test. `fromEnvironment` reads it from `MASK_SENSITIVE_HEADERS`.

## Operations — how to call one

- **Positional arguments.** Every operation is `client.<controller>.<operation>(arg1, arg2, ..., requestOptions?)`. Order matters; there is no options object. Pass `undefined` to skip an optional argument and reach a later one. Each operation block gives the full order in **Signature** and in the `#` column.
- **`idempotencyKey` moves.** In the 11 operations whose body is optional, `idempotencyKey` comes **before** `body` (`client.charges.createCharge(idempotencyKey?, body?)`); in the 14 whose body is required it comes after (`client.refunds.createRefund(storeId, chargeId, body, idempotencyKey?)`).
- **What comes back.** Every operation returns `Promise<ApiResponse<T>>`: `{ request, statusCode, headers, result, body }`. `result` is the parsed model; `body` is the raw response text.
- **Per-call options.** The last argument is `RequestOptions`, which has one field: `abortSignal`. The type is not exported from the package, so write it inline: `{ abortSignal: controller.signal }`. Aborting rejects with `AbortError` (exported).
- **Server.** Each block names its server: `default` uses `baseUrl`; `directDebit` (the 14 direct debit operations) uses `directDebitBaseUrl`.
- **Auth.** All 73 operations send `Authorization: Bearer <secretKey>.<jwtToken>`. There is no per-call override.

Headers, as listed in each block's **Headers sent** line:

| Header | When | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `authorization` | every call | `Bearer <secretKey>.<jwtToken>` |
| `user-agent` | every call | the fixed text `TypeScript-SDK/1.2.3 (OS: {os-info}, Engine: {engine}/{engine-version})` — the placeholders are sent unfilled |
| `accept` | every call | `application/json` when the operation returns a model; `application/json, text/plain, */*` (axios default) when it returns nothing |
| `content-type` | POST and PATCH | `application/json` when the operation has a body argument — **also when you leave an optional body out** (then no body is sent, but the header is); `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` (axios default, empty body) for the two POST/PATCH operations with no body argument |
| `idempotency-key` | POST and PATCH (28 operations) | your `idempotencyKey` argument; when you leave it out, or the operation has no such argument, the client sends a **new random UUID v4 on every call**. GET and DELETE never get one |

The random key comes from the hand-written interceptor in `src/extensions.ts`. It protects one call's retries (the same key is reused across that call's retry attempts), but **not** your own repeat of a call: calling again makes a new key. To make a repeat safe, create the key yourself and pass it.

How values go on the wire:

- **Path**: each value is percent-encoded into its segment (`a/b` becomes `a%2Fb`).
- **Query**: a boolean is `true`/`false`. Unset optional parameters leave empty `&` separators behind (`?&&&metadata=m`).
- **Query arrays**: each item is sent as `key[]=value`. Five transaction-history filters already have `[]` in their wire name, so they go out as `card_brand[][]=visa`, `brand[][]`, `brands[][]`, `service_providers[][]` and `bank_transfer_payment_statuses[][]`. **Live test: `card_brand[][]=visa` returned 0 items where `card_brand[]=visa` returned 50**, so the `cardBrand` filter does not work through the SDK. The other four were not tested live.
- **JSON body**: field names are mapped to their wire names (model tables); see Models for unknown keys and `bigint`.

How to read an operation block:

- **Call**: the call with every argument; `?` marks optional ones.
- **Signature**: the exact TypeScript signature.
- **Wire**: HTTP method and path. `{name}` in the path is filled from the argument of that name.
- **Request body**, **Headers sent**, **Idempotency-Key**, **Returns**, **Client shortcut**, **Types** (links to the model tables).
- The parameter table: `#` = position, `SDK name` = argument name, `Wire name` = the query key, header name, path placeholder or `(JSON body)`, `In` = where it goes, `Type`, `Required`.
- The error table: see the next section.

- **Paging.** Every list operation except `listBankTransferLedgers` takes `limit`, `cursor` and `cursorDirection`; every list result has `items` and `hasMore`. For the next page, call again with the same `limit` and `cursor` = the `id` of the last item you got (their doc comment: "the resource after which pagination should continue"); stop when `hasMore` is `false`. Live test on `listStoreCharges`: two pages of 5 gave the same 10 ids, in order, as one call with `limit` 10.

## Error model

Operations throw. What you can catch:

| Thrown | When | What is on it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ExternalApiError` (extends `ApiError`) | a non-2xx status that has an `ExternalApiError` row in the operation's error table | `statusCode`, `headers`, `body` (raw text), `request`, and `result` = the response body parsed as JSON (not checked against a schema; `undefined` when the body is not JSON or empty) |
| `ApiError` | every other non-2xx status | the same fields, but **`result` is always `undefined`** — read `error.body` |
| `ResponseValidationError` | a 2xx body that does not fit the response model: a wrong type, a missing required field, or an enum value the SDK does not list | `statusCode`, `body`, `errors`. Not an `ApiError` |
| `ArgumentsValidationError` | an argument that does not fit its type (for example an enum value that is not listed, or a string where a number is expected); **nothing is sent** | the failing argument's name **and the given value** in `message` (card data included, see Models) |
| plain `Error` "Could not parse body as JSON ..." | an empty or non-JSON 2xx body on an operation that returns a model | — |
| plain `Error` from a client shortcut | the app token has no `store_id` (or `merchant_id`) claim; nothing is sent | see Client shortcuts |
| axios error (`error.isAxiosError === true`) | no HTTP answer: `error.code` is `ECONNABORTED` after `timeout`, `ECONNREFUSED` when nothing listens | not an `ApiError`; the class is not exported |
| `AbortError` | your `abortSignal` fired | not an `ApiError` |

`ApiError`, `ExternalApiError`, `ResponseValidationError`, `ArgumentsValidationError` and `AbortError` are exported from the package root.

**The error table in each operation block.** Rows are tried top to bottom and the first matching status wins. `Class thrown` is the exact class (`error.constructor`). The `error.message` column uses two placeholders:

- `<code>` is the body's `code` field **written as JSON**: a string keeps its double quotes (`HTTP 404 Not Found: "INVALID_PATH_VALUE"`), a number is bare. When the body is empty, not JSON, or has no `code`, `<code>` is empty (`HTTP 404 Not Found: `). The live API answers an unknown charge id with a 404 and an **empty** body.
- The last row, "any other non-2xx", shows its message **as the SDK writes it**: the text `HTTP {$statusCode}: {$response.body#/code}` is not filled in.
- Three operations — `createSubscription`, `listAllSubscriptions`, `listStoreSubscriptions` — have no error rows at all: every non-2xx is an `ApiError` with message `Response status code was not ok: <status>.` and `result` `undefined`.
- **Reading the error code.** `ExternalApiError` rows exist only for 400, 401, 403 and 404 (which of these depends on the operation). On the 70 operations that have rows, **409 and 429 are always plain `ApiError`**, so `error.result` is `undefined` for them — `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT` and rate limits only reach you through the body. To read the code from any `ApiError`, parse the body yourself: `JSON.parse(error.body).code` (guard the parse: the body can be empty).

```ts
import { ApiError, ExternalApiError, ResponseValidationError, ArgumentsValidationError, AbortError, Client } from 'univapay-client-sdk';

declare const client: Client;

try {
  const { result } = await client.refunds.getRefund('storeId', 'chargeId', 'refundId');
  console.log(result.status);
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof ExternalApiError) {
    // parsed body, when it was JSON: error.result?.code, error.result?.errors
    console.log(error.statusCode, error.result?.code);
  } else if (error instanceof ApiError) {
    // result is always undefined here: parse error.body yourself
    console.log(error.statusCode, error.body);
  } else if (error instanceof ResponseValidationError || error instanceof ArgumentsValidationError || error instanceof AbortError) {
    console.log(error.message);
  } else {
    throw error; // axios errors (timeout, no connection) and plain Errors
  }
}
```

`ExternalApiError.result` is typed as the error body model: `status`, `code`, `errors?: ApiErrorDetail[]` and `additionalProperties` (source: `src/errors/externalApiError.ts`; `ApiErrorDetail` is in [map/models/common.md](map/models/common.md#apierrordetail)).

## Models

Each model has one table on one page under `map/models/`; the operation blocks link to it. Import every model name from `univapay-client-sdk`. The schemas (`refundSchema` and so on) are not exported.

- **Object tables**: `SDK field` is the TypeScript property, `Wire name` is the JSON key, `Type` is the declared type, `Optional` says whether the property is declared with `?`.
- **Enum tables**: each enum is a TypeScript `enum`; `Member` is what you write, `Wire value` is what is sent and received.
- **Union tables**: the arms, and the type guards the SDK exports for them (for example `TransactionToken.isCardTransactionToken(value)`).

Behaviour that is the same for every model:

- **Closed enums.** Only the listed values are accepted. A response with any other value (for example a new status the API adds) fails the **whole** response with `ResponseValidationError`. Passing an unlisted value as an argument fails with `ArgumentsValidationError` before anything is sent — **except inside the `TransactionTokenCreateRequestData` union** (the `data` of `createTransactionToken`), see below.
- **Wrong types fail the whole response too** (metadata values are the exception, see below). Example: `GenericMetadata.orderId` is a `string`, so a response whose `metadata.order_id` is a number (one charge in a list is enough) throws `ResponseValidationError`.
- **Unknown keys in a response** are kept in `additionalProperties`, under their wire names: `{ id, additionalProperties: { brand_new_field: 1 } }`. Every object model has this field; its type is in the table header.
- **Unknown keys in a request.** Keys you put in `additionalProperties` are sent as plain JSON keys, exactly as written. A key that is not a field and not inside `additionalProperties` is also sent exactly as written — it is **not** converted to snake_case.
- **Metadata.** `GenericMetadata` maps `orderId` ↔ `order_id`, `univapayName` ↔ `univapay-name` and `univapayPhoneNumber` ↔ `univapay-phone-number`. Every other metadata key travels in `metadata.additionalProperties`, both ways. **Metadata values must be a string, number, boolean, `null`, or an array of those.** In `GenericMetadata` (charges, refunds, cancels, subscriptions, transaction history) a value that is an object, or an array holding an object, is **dropped with no error**, on read and on send. Transaction-token metadata (`Record<string, TransactionTokenMetadataAdditionalProperties>`) is stricter: the same value fails the **whole** response with `ResponseValidationError`.
- **null and missing keys, on read.** A JSON `null` on a field whose type has no `null` becomes `undefined`. On a field typed `... | null` it stays `null`. A missing key is accepted when the field is optional or its type includes `null`; a missing required field fails with `ResponseValidationError`.
- **`bigint`.** The direct debit `amount` fields are `bigint`. Pass a `bigint` (a `number` is also accepted at run time); it is sent as an exact JSON number, and read back as a `bigint`.
- **`WebhookTrigger.TokenThreeDSUpdated` is `token_three_d_s_updated`** in this SDK. The enum is closed, so no other spelling can be sent through `createWebhook` / `updateWebhook`, and a stored webhook whose triggers include a value the enum does not list fails to read with `ResponseValidationError`.
- **`TransactionTokenCreateRequestData` (request union, `anyOf`)**: its arms are tried in the table's order and the first one that fits is used, field names included. An online-payment `data` whose `brand`, `callMethod` or `osType` is not a listed value is **not rejected**: it fits `TokenCreateBankTransferData` (which only needs `brand: string`) and goes out with its other keys unconverted (`callMethod`, `userIdentifier` in camelCase). Check online values against `BaseOnlineDataBrand`, `BaseOnlineDataCallMethod` and `BaseOnlineDataOsType` yourself before sending.
- **Card dates are strings.** `TokenCreateCardData.expMonth` and `expYear` are `string`. Numbers fail before sending with `ArgumentsValidationError` ("Argument for 'body' failed validation. Could not match against any acceptable type ... Path: data"): it points at `data`, not at the field. **The message repeats the given value, so the card number and CVV are in it** — do not log `error.message` from `createTransactionToken` as is.
- **The `TransactionToken` union** is picked by the `payment_type` value in the response, per its table.

## Poll helpers

Hand-written in `src/extensions.ts` and attached to four controllers at run time: `charges.pollCharge(storeId, id, maxAttempts?, requestOptions?)`, `refunds.pollRefund(storeId, chargeId, id, maxAttempts?, requestOptions?)`, `cancels.pollCancel(storeId, chargeId, id, maxAttempts?, requestOptions?)`, `subscriptions.pollSubscription(storeId, id, maxAttempts?, requestOptions?)`. `maxAttempts` defaults to `10`.

- **They are missing from the published types.** `client.charges.pollCharge(...)` fails to compile (TS2339) because the package's `.d.ts` files never load `extensions.d.ts`. They work at run time. Typed ways in: the client shortcuts `client.pollCharge(chargeId, ...)`, `client.pollRefund(chargeId, id, ...)`, `client.pollCancel(chargeId, id, ...)`, `client.pollSubscription(id, ...)` (store-level token), or a cast such as `(client.charges as any).pollCharge(...)`.
- **`pollCharge`** first reads the charge once without `polling`. If the status is final (`successful`, `failed`, `error`, `canceled`) it returns that response. Otherwise it repeats `GET ...?polling=true` up to `maxAttempts` times and stops at the first status reachable from the starting one (from `pending`: `awaiting`, `authorized`, `successful`, `failed`, `error`, `canceled`; from `awaiting`: the same minus `awaiting`; from `authorized`: `successful`, `failed`, `error`, `canceled`).
- **`pollRefund` and `pollCancel`** repeat `GET ...?polling=true` up to `maxAttempts` times until the status is `successful`, `failed` or `error`. **`pollSubscription`** does the same until the status is anything but `unverified`. When the attempts run out, these three make **one more** GET and return it.
- When the attempts run out, every helper **resolves** with the last response — no error. Check `result.status` yourself.
- The helpers do not wait between requests; the waiting is done by the server, which holds a `polling=true` request open. An error status ends the poll with the usual error.
- **Measured once, not a rule** (test mode, store-level token, 2026-11-26, from this machine): `getCharge(..., true)` on charges already `successful`, `canceled` or `failed` answered in 0.6–0.8 s. The hold time for a `pending` or `awaiting` charge was not measured here. With the default `maxAttempts` of 10, the total wait is up to ten such holds.

## Client shortcuts

Hand-written in `src/client.ts`: 51 methods on `client` itself that read the store id (and, for `listSubscriptionCharges`, also the merchant id) from the app token, then call the controller method with the remaining arguments in the same order and return its response unchanged. Each operation page lists its shortcuts with their signatures.

- They need a **store-level** app token. With a merchant-level token (no `store_id` claim) or no token, the call returns a **rejected promise** with a plain `Error` — for example `getCharge(chargeId) requires a store-level App Token: the configured token carries no usable "store_id" claim. Use a store-level App Token, or call getCharge(storeId, chargeId) on ChargesApi with an explicit store id.` Nothing is sent.
- `listSubscriptionCharges(subscriptionId, ...)` checks `merchant_id` first, then `store_id`.

---

## Webhook handlers

The SDK exports one handler per event group: `ChargeHandler`, `TokenHandler`, `RefundHandler`, `CancelHandler`, `SubscriptionHandler`, `BankTransferHandler`, `CustomsHandler`, each with `parseEvent(request)`, and a matching `...ParsingResult` namespace of type guards. The payload models are on [map/models/webhook-payloads.md](map/models/webhook-payloads.md).

```ts
import { ChargeHandler, ChargeParsingResult } from 'univapay-client-sdk';

declare const rawBody: string;

const handler = new ChargeHandler();
const request: Parameters<ChargeHandler['parseEvent']>[0] = {
  method: 'POST',
  url: '/webhooks/univapay',
  headers: {},
  body: { type: 'text', content: rawBody },
};
const event = handler.parseEvent(request);
if (ChargeParsingResult.isEventTypeUnknown(event)) {
  console.log(event.body); // the raw body text
}
```

- **Real deliveries come back as unknown.** The payload models require `id` and `created_on`; a delivery that carries only `event` and `data` (the shape of the test-mode deliveries captured for this project) is returned as an `UnknownEvent`, whose `body` is the raw text. Parse `JSON.parse(rawBody)` yourself and switch on `event`.
- **The guards test shape only.** For a parsed charge event, `isChargeUpdatedEvent` and `isChargeFinishedEvent` are both true. Read `event.event` instead.
- The request type for `parseEvent` is not exported; `Parameters<ChargeHandler['parseEvent']>[0]` names it, as above.

## Runtime & packaging

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Node | `engines.node` is `>=14.17.0` |
| CommonJS | `require('univapay-client-sdk')` works |
| Plain Node ESM | **`import ... from 'univapay-client-sdk'` fails** in plain Node (tested on Node 22.14): `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, because the 14 webhook handler files in `dist/esm/events/webhooks/` import other files without `.js` (the rest of `dist/esm` uses `.js`); the package root loads them, so every import of the root fails. From an ES module, load it with `createRequire(import.meta.url)('univapay-client-sdk')`; from CommonJS, `require` it |
| Package entries | only the root works. Deep imports (`univapay-client-sdk/dist/...`) fail with `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`; the declared `univapay-client-sdk/metadata` entry has no files (`MODULE_NOT_FOUND`) |
| TypeScript | the `.d.ts` files reference Node types (`NodeJS`, `stream`): install `@types/node` **and**, under `module: "commonjs"`, enable `esModuleInterop` (without it `tsc` fails with TS1259 on `form-data` in `@apimatic/axios-client-adapter`) — or set `skipLibCheck: true`. In an ES-module file (`.mts`, or `"type": "module"`) with `moduleResolution` `node16`/`nodenext`, the package's ESM `.d.ts` files fail with TS2834 (imports without extensions): set `skipLibCheck: true`, or use `moduleResolution: "bundler"` |
| Not exported | `RequestOptions` (type), `HttpRequest`, the model schemas, `isUnknownEvent`, the axios error class |
| Dependencies | `@apimatic/*` runtime packages with `^` ranges — pin them with a lockfile |
